builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SkillBridge: Cost-Aware Diagnosis and Repair of Cross-OS Compatibility Defects in Agent Skills
summary: It replaces running every skill on every OS (or uniformly sampling executions) with a three-stage contract workflow: static screening for OS-sensitive evidence, targeted dynamic validation, and field-level repair of guide text, scripts, dependencies, or platform declarations. Costs are an added static-analysis and root-cause-review pipeline, plus residual dynamic runs; the absolute pass rate after repair remains only 38.4%, so most tasks still fail reviewer judgment. It can fail where OS assumptions are not visible in contract fields (runtime-only behaviors), where static evidence misprioritizes cases, and where repairs fix one platform while regressing another, since no cross-platform regression check is quantified.
rationale: A small team shipping cross-OS agent skills can trial the static-then-dynamic triage pattern cheaply, but the gains are reported on one 1,090-skill corpus and must be revalidated on their own skill inventory.

claims.statement: It replaces running every skill on every OS (or uniformly sampling executions) with a three-stage contract workflow: static screening for OS-sensitive evidence, targeted dynamic validation, and field-level repair of guide text, scripts, dependencies, or platform declarations. Costs are an added static-analysis and root-cause-review pipeline, plus residual dynamic runs; the absolute pass rate after repair remains only 38.4%, so most tasks still fail reviewer judgment. It can fail where OS assumptions are not visible in contract fields (runtime-only behaviors), where static evidence misprioritizes cases, and where repairs fix one platform while regressing another, since no cross-platform regression check is quantified.
SkillBridge confirms 38 OS issues with 185 dynamic validations versus roughly 865 for uniform random selection, and repair raises reviewer-judged pass rate from 30.6% to 38.4% (+7.8 points).
